prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: individual Bible Journey illustration of Paul’s literary comparison in 1 Corinthians 12:12–27, landscape 1536×1024, full frame, no interface or text.
Input images: Image 1 and Image 2 are approved style references only. Match their warm cinematic realism, natural proportions, tactile materials, nuanced light, and respectful storytelling. Do not reproduce their scenes, characters, or compositions.
Scene/backdrop: One unlocated community gathering used to illustrate Paul’s comparison of one body with many members. This is not a documented historical event or a claim about a specific church meeting.
Subject/action: Show a small group of distinct, fully clothed ordinary people who belong together. Their faces and ages vary naturally; no one is a copy or a stand-in for a named person. One member sits comfortably while companions make room, gently offer a hand, and respond with attentive, caring expressions. Keep them visibly separate human beings with ordinary intact bodies; this illustrates mutual care, not anatomical parts.
Composition/framing: Use a medium-wide view from several paces away; the group should occupy about 60% of the canvas height, not fill the frame vertically. Show the figures from waist or knee up, with all heads fully visible and their hair beginning below the 18% line; keep the group’s lower edge above the 85% line. Do not crop any head, hand, or caring interaction at a frame edge. Place the whole group within the left 60%; reserve the right 30% as quiet, low-detail wall and open floor for a reading panel. Leave visible space above the heads and below the group. One continuous scene.
Style/materials: Warm cinematic realistic illustration; simple period-evocative woven garments without assigning identities, tactile cloth and wood, natural expressive faces and hands, restrained earth pigments, soft natural light.
Constraints: This is an editorial visual aid for Paul’s body-and-members comparison, not a historical scene. No hybrid bodies, floating body parts, gore, rank insignia, disability stereotypes, text, labels, captions, writing, symbols, banners, maps, modern objects, pins, logos, border, or watermark.
notes: Final raster reviewed against the named subjects; account-specific references remain in the scene registry. Historical appearances are reconstructed and literary scenes are labeled.
